xmldoc.short_description: The guided tour: run the whole module end to end and say what it found.

param_input_item.param_description: options as name and value pairs, matched without regard to case: Record (a recording from a reader or ecglab.simulate, a file path, or a 'database/record' name for ecglab.reference; '' by default, which simulates a recording), Seconds (the length of the simulated recording; default 30, used only when Record is ''), Seed (the seed of the simulated recording; default 7, used only when Record is ''), Detector (the beat detector the analysis uses; default 'pantompkins'), Draw (draw and save the three reading pages; false by default), OutputDir (where the pages are saved when Draw is true; default the temporary directory), Visible ('off' by default, or 'on'), Language ('en' by default, or 'fr' for French without accents).

param_output_item.param_description: the analysis from ecglab.analyze (kind 'ecglab.analysis'). With no output argument the tour is printed and nothing is returned.
the tour as a char array with newlines, when a second output is asked for.

description.p: The guided tour is the one call that shows what ecglab does. It takes a recording, runs the whole analysis chain with ecglab.analyze (clean, quality, detect, delineate, classify, rhythm, heart rate variability, twelve-lead measurements), narrates in one line each what every stage found, and ends by printing the study report of ecglab.report. With no Record it simulates a twelve-lead recording, so the tour runs anywhere, with no file and no network, and the leads, the frontal axis and the global intervals all run.

Every number the tour narrates is one ecglab.analyze produced; the tour recomputes nothing. Its text, like the report, opens with the research-only disclaimer, so the tour is never read without the sentence that this is not a medical device.

When Draw is true the tour also draws and saves the three reading pages, the calibrated strip (ecglab.strip), the summary chart (ecglab.chart) and the one-beat view (ecglab.beat), and names the files it wrote. Drawing needs an advanced-CLI session with a figure; by default the tour is a headless call that prints and draws nothing.

With no output argument the tour is printed and nothing is returned; with an output argument the analysis is returned and nothing is printed, so the tour can be run for a person or captured by a program.

Research software, not a medical device. ecglab is for research and education. It is not a medical device and must not be used for clinical diagnosis, patient monitoring, treatment decisions, or any medical purpose.

example_item.example_item_data: % Run the guided tour on a simulated recording and print it. ecglab.demo();
